examples.label: disk group - raw filesystem read via debugfs
adm group - read all system logs

notes: disk group = raw read of the block device with debugfs (read any file, including /etc/shadow). adm group = read every file under /var/log, which often leaks creds and tokens.

recommended.note: Confirms which privileged group you're in.
Mine the readable logs/files for creds.

name: Privileged Groups - disk and adm Groups
description: The disk group grants raw block-device access via debugfs - read any file including /etc/shadow and root's SSH key. The adm group can read all system logs, often exposing credentials.

defense.why_it_works: Members of the 'disk' group can access raw block devices (/dev/sda, /dev/sdb). debugfs provides filesystem-level access to block devices, allowing reading of any file on the disk including /etc/shadow, SSH keys, and /root/ contents -- bypassing filesystem permission checks entirely since access is at the block level.
defense.prerequisites: Attacker's user is a member of the 'disk' group. debugfs tool installed. Raw block device accessible.
defense.impact: Full read access to any file on the system disk, including /etc/shadow (for offline password cracking), /root/.ssh/id_rsa, database files, and any other sensitive data -- without needing root-level sudo.
defense.detection: debugfs executed by a disk-group member. Raw block device access by non-root. Auditd: open(/dev/sda) by non-root user.
defense.artifacts: Auditd: debugfs accessing /dev/sda | Process log: debugfs opened by non-root | Block device access log
defense.prevention: Remove users from the 'disk' group unless strictly required for operational purposes. Audit group memberships regularly. Treat disk group membership as equivalent to root access.
defense.misconfiguration: Regular users added to the 'disk' group without understanding that it provides raw disk access equivalent to root read access on the filesystem.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# User in disk group
id
# uid=1000(htb-student) groups=...,6(disk)

# debugfs unrestricted
debugfs /dev/sda1  # gives filesystem-level read
defense.secure_config:
# Audit and remove unnecessary group memberships
getent group disk
gpasswd -d htb-student disk

# Periodic audit
awk -F: '$4 ~ /(disk|docker|lxd|sudo|adm)/' /etc/group

# Use minimal group assignment -- principle of least privilege
